subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get their own tool-policy layer, and should that layer be an explicit `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` contract or inheritance from `tools.subagents.tools`?
rationale: This decides a new security/default boundary for scheduled automation and message delivery, including upgrade behavior for existing cron jobs that may intentionally use `message`.

options.title: Add explicit cron policy
options.body: Define `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, then add focused cron/message-delivery tests.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron sessions as inheriting `tools.subagents.tools`, accepting the compatibility risk that existing scheduled jobs may lose tools under a policy originally named for subagents.

options.title: Keep per-job policy only
options.body: Decline the global cron config surface and document `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery-mode guidance as the supported restriction mechanism.

recommendation.title: Add explicit cron policy
recommendation.body: Define `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, then add focused cron/message-delivery tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-history signal across the config/tool-policy paths and prior review context for this security-sensitive cron policy decision.
